questions.stem: During the electrolysis of molten lead bromide, what forms at the anode?
questions.explanation: At the anode (positive electrode), the bromide ions (Br⁻) are attracted and lose electrons (oxidation): 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻. This produces orange/brown bromine vapour. Lead metal forms at the cathode, where Pb²⁺ ions gain electrons.
